sentences.text: JUDGMENT Easwaran S., J.
The judgment of ours shall dispose of four appeals.
Three are preferred by the claimants and one is preferred by the State.
2. Facts of the appeal preferred by the state is narrated first.
LA. Appeal No.83 of 2021:
An extent of 8.09 Ares of land was acquired for the purpose of widening of Gandhi Road - Mini Bye Pass Block No.4 as per 4(1) notification dated 18.01.2011.

The Land Acquisition Officer fixed the land value at Rs.6,39,508/-
per cent.
Dissatisfied with the value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the claimant sought reference under Section 18 of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

It was contended by the claimant that the land was acquired surrounded by several important institutions and establishments including Providence Higher Secondary School, St.Joseph's Primary School,
Malabar Christian College, MES Women's College, and Sanmarga Darshini Library.

It was further contended that several Government institutions like Nadakkavu Head Post Office, Vellayil Post Office, KSEB Office, etc., were situated near the acquired land and the other National Highway,
namely, Wayanad Road passes through the other end of the Malabar Christian College compound.
The claimant in support of the claim produced Exts.A1 to A69 documents, and AW1 was examined in support of the claim.
On behalf of the State, no oral or LA.APP. NOs. 336 & 323 OF 2016 9 2024:KER:91771 LA.APP. NO. 120 OF 2017 & LA.APP. NO. 83 OF 2021 documentary evidence was adduced.
The claimant further sought for the appointment of an Advocate Commissioner for local inspection, and the Advocate Commissioner submitted his report, which was marked as Ext.CI.
An additional report was also sought for, which was marked as Exts.C2 and C3.
The sketch prepared by the Advocate Commissioner was produced and marked as C1(a), C2(a), and C3(a).

The reference court on the basis of the evidence on record framed the following issues:-

sentences.text: 2) Whether the claimant is entitled to get enhancement in structural value?
3) Whether the claimant is entitled to get compensation for injurious affection to the remaining property?

4) Reliefs and costs?
3.

On analysis of this evidence, the reference court rendered the finding that in respect of the same acquisition, the reference court in connected cases, namely, LAR Nos.22/14, 98/14, 99/14 100/14,
and 107/14 had fixed the land value at Rs.12,00,000/- per cent.
Based on the aforesaid findings, the reference court proceeded to consider the claim raised by the claimant.
The reference court further found that the land acquired was abutting NH 17 Kannur Road.

Therefore, the reference court enhanced the compensation to Rs.14,00,000/- per cent by taking the base value fixed by the reference court in the connected LA.APP. NOs. 336 & 323 OF 2016 10 2024:KER:91771 LA.APP.
NO. 120 OF 2017 & LA.APP. NO. 83 OF 2021 references.
It is aggrieved by the fixation of the land value by the reference court, the State has come up in the present appeal.
LA.APP.

4.
These appeals are preferred by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation in respect of the land acquired by the very same notification.
In LA.
APP. No. 336 of 2016
, an extent of 0.0035 hectares of garden land in T.S. No.5-19-912/2 of Kasaba Village, was acquired.
In LA.

No. 323 of 2016
, the extent of land acquired was 0.0050 hectares of garden land in T.S. No.5-19- 907/2 of Kasaba Village.
In LA.
APP. No 120 of 2017, the extent of land acquired is 0.0034 hectares of garden land in T.S. No.5-19-908/3 of Kasaba Village.
The Land Acquisition Officer fixed the land value at Rs.6,39,250/-.
The reference court by relying upon the judgment in LAR No.259/2014 enhanced the compensation to Rs.9,58,875/- per cent.
Aggrieved by the aforesaid fixation, the claimants have approached this Court.
5. We have heard Sri. T.K.Shajahan the learned Senior Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the appellants in LA.
APP. No. 83 of 2021 and respondent State in LA.
APP. No. 336 & 323 of 2016 and LA.
App. No. 120 of 2017, Sri.Rajan Vishnuraj, the learned counsel appearing for the appellants in LA.
App. No. 336 & 323 of 2016, and Sri.M.Promodh Kumar, the learned counsel appearing for the appellants in LA.
App. No. 120 of 2017.

6. The learned Senior Government Pleader for the State primarily contended that the land value fixed by the reference court at Rs.14,00,000/-

sentences.text:
He would further submit that even if the reference court was of the opinion that the claimant was entitled to fixation of the higher value than fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer,
the reference court could not have gone beyond the value fixed in the connected Land Acquisition references answered by the court.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimants would submit that the land acquired in respect of the claimants, who are in appeal before this Court is abutting the Mavoor Road, the expansion for which the acquisition was notified.

With reference to the sketch prepared by the Advocate Commissioner, Learned Counsels tried to impress upon us with reference to the sketch prepared by the advocate commissioner, the exact lie of the property.

Still, further, it is contended that Ext.A1 sale deed dated 27.03.2007 having an extent of 33.08 cents was purchased for an amount of Rs.16,57,871/- per cent and the very same property was again sold in 03.03.2011 for a sum of Rs.21,81,253/- per cent.
Therefore, the learned counsels submitted that the reference court ought to have fixed either of these two values for the purpose of arriving at the market value of the land acquired.
8. We have considered the rival submissions made across the bar.
9. The perusal of the impugned judgment of the reference court in LAR.No.325 of 2014 reveals that the commercial importance of the property has been rightly appreciated by the reference court.

Even otherwise, the LA.APP. NOs. 336 & 323 OF 2016 12 2024:KER:91771 LA.APP. NO. 120 OF 2017 & LA.APP. NO. 83 OF 2021 learned Senior Government Pleader appearing for the State do not deny the commercial importance of the land but submits that while fixing the value of the land acquired, parity in compensation ought to have been applied with reference to the judgment of the reference court in LAR No.22 of 2014 and connected cases.
10. A perusal of the plan and the sketch prepared by the Advocate Commissioner reveals the exact lie of the land acquired in respect of the claimants in LA.
App. Nos.323 and 326 of 2016 and LA.
App. No.120 of 2017.
It is pertinent to mention that the land acquired is situated within a distance of 100 metres from the land covered by the Ext.A1 document.
Therefore, it is clear that neither the Land Acquisition Officer nor the reference court has considered the relevance of the Ext.A1 document in its true perspective.
11. However, having said so, we find that the property covered by Ext.A1 has an extent of 33.08 cents.
The value fixed in Ext.A1, thus being for a larger extent, we are of the view that the holder of the property was in a more advantageous position.
Therefore, it will not be expeditious for us to rely on the value fixed per cent in Ext.A1 inorder to arrive at just compensation in respect of the land acquired in the present case.
But at the same time, the land owners are also required to get adequate compensation for the land, which has been acquired from them.

12. Considering the totality, the facts and circumstances, when we analyze the findings of the reference court in LAR No.325 of 2014 and also the LA.APP. NOs. 336 & 323 OF 2016 13 2024:KER:91771 LA.APP. NO. 120 OF 2017 & LA.APP. NO. 83 OF 2021 exact lie of the property in the other appeals

, we are of the considered view that the reference court has rightly fixed the value Vilasini vs The District Collector, Kozhikode on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73891116/
8 for the land acquired in LAR. No.325 of 2014 in Rs.14,00,000/-.

sentences.text: Therefore, we see no merit in the appeal preferred by the State and accordingly the same is dismissed.

13. Since we have found that the value arrived by the reference court in LAR No.325 of 2014 is correct, the claimants in LAR No.312 of 2014 and LAR No.344 of 2014, and LAR No.259 of 2014 are also entitled to the parity of compensation because their property is also similarly situated as revealed from the report and plan of the Advocate Commissioner, we are of the considered view that the amount of Rs.14,00,000/- can be fixed as the land value in respect of the land in question.
14. Before parting with the case, we need to address the claim of the appellant in LA.App.No. 120 of 2017 for severance compensation.

A perusal of the Judgment impugned shows that the claim for severance compensation was not considered at all probably because the claimant failed to adduce any evidence in support of his claim for severance compensation.
In the absence of the evidence we are not inclined to grant any compensation under the said head.
15. As an upshot of our discussions, we are of the view that LA.App. Nos.323 and 326 of 2016 and LA.App. No.120 of 2017 are liable to be allowed to the extent indicated above.

The land value in respect of the land acquired in the respective references would stand enhanced to Rs.14,00,000/-
per cent.

The claimants are also entitled to all statutory benefits flowing out of the fixation of the land value as indicated above including proportionate cost in the appeal.
Ordered accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, it is clear that neither the Land Acquisition Officer nor the reference court has considered the relevance of the Ext.A1 document in its true perspective.
11. However, having said so, we find that the property covered by Ext.A1 has an extent of 33.08 cents.
The value fixed in Ext.A1, thus being for a larger extent, we are of the view that the holder of the property was in a more advantageous position.
Therefore, it will not be expeditious for us to rely on the value fixed per cent in Ext.A1 inorder to arrive at just compensation in respect of the land acquired in the present case.
But at the same time, the land owners are also required to get adequate compensation for the land, which has been acquired from them.
12. Considering the totality, the facts and circumstances, when we analyze the findings of the reference court in LAR No.325 of 2014 and also the LA.APP. NOs. 336 & 323 OF 2016 13 2024:KER:91771 LA.APP. NO. 120 OF 2017 & LA.APP. NO. 83 OF 2021 exact lie of the property in the other appeals
, we are of the considered view that the reference court has rightly fixed the value Vilasini vs The District Collector, Kozhikode on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73891116/
8 for the land acquired in LAR. No.325 of 2014 in Rs.14,00,000/-.
13. Since we have found that the value arrived by the reference court in LAR No.325 of 2014 is correct, the claimants in LAR No.312 of 2014 and LAR No.344 of 2014, and LAR No.259 of 2014 are also entitled to the parity of compensation because their property is also similarly situated as revealed from the report and plan of the Advocate Commissioner, we are of the considered view that the amount of Rs.14,00,000/- can be fixed as the land value in respect of the land in question.
A perusal of the Judgment impugned shows that the claim for severance compensation was not considered at all probably because the claimant failed to adduce any evidence in support of his claim for severance compensation.
